		<item>
		<title>Patrick Dougherty&#8217;s &#8216;Stickwork&#8217; Installations Conjure Connections with Nature</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/patrick-dougherty-stickwork-public-sculpture-willow-saplings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 23 Jul 2026 15:22:44 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Design]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[architecture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art environments]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[environment]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[immersive]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Patrick Dougherty]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[public art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[trees]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wood]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476089</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-8.jpeg" alt="Patrick Dougherty&#8217;s &#8216;Stickwork&#8217; Installations Conjure Connections with Nature" />For more than four decades, the artist has reimagined the technical and sculptural capabilities of one simple material: twigs.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/patrick-dougherty-stickwork-public-sculpture-willow-saplings/">Patrick Dougherty&#8217;s &#8216;Stickwork&#8217; Installations Conjure Connections with Nature</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-8.jpeg" alt="Patrick Dougherty&#8217;s &#8216;Stickwork&#8217; Installations Conjure Connections with Nature" />


<p>For more than four decades, environmental artist <a href="https://www.stickwork.net/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Patrick Dougherty</a> has reimagined the technical and sculptural capabilities of one simple material: twigs. Over the years, the North Carolina-based artist completed well over 300 large-scale, site-specific installations in a series he calls <em>Stickworks,</em> using literal truckloads of willow saplings from specialized farms in Canada that grow them for applications like fencing, basketmaking, and more. Where possible, Dougherty has also incorporated materials the local area had to offer.</p>



<p>I first stumbled upon the artist&#8217;s whimsical constructions in Door County, Wisconsin, where &#8220;Happy Go Lucky&#8221; sits at Horseshoe Bay Farms near Egg Harbor. By the time I experienced the work, it had already been colonized by Virginia creeper vines, which turn bright red in the autumn. The piece is simultaneously structural and fantastical, providing an inviting armature for nature, including insects.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1506" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11.jpg" alt="a public art sculpture in the forest made from interwoven twigs and saplings" class="wp-image-476100" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11-640x482.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11-960x723.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11-768x578.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-11-1536x1157.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;The Jealous Wall.&#8221; Image courtesy of Docent</figcaption></figure>



<p>Some of Dougherty&#8217;s public installations take architectural forms consisting of arches and towers, such as &#8220;Sea Change&#8221; and &#8220;Rough &#8216;n Tumble.&#8221; &#8220;All in the Family&#8221; resembles a group of larger-than-life urns. And others lean into a sense that the forest is always in a state of reclaiming. &#8220;The Jealous Wall&#8221; is constructed around existing buildings, as if the saplings are growing in slow motion and and engulfing everything in its path, not unlike the way nature, left to its own devices, will always redeem its space. All of his works emphasize an invitation, as visitors are encouraged to walk around and through the sculptures.</p>



<p>Pieces created over the past decade or so also bear the signature of artist Sam Dougherty, who provided full-time assistance in addition to his own <a href="https://samdoughertypottery.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">pottery practice</a>. Semi-retired now, Patrick Dougherty is still making works in his studio, and a recent exhibition at the <a href="https://www.blowingrockmuseum.org/exhibitions" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Brahm Blowing Rock Art &amp; History Museum</a> included a wall-to-wall display of gloves collected over the years and signed by the volunteers who helped to install the works. Explore more from the archive on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.stickwork.net/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">website</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6.jpg" alt="a whimsical, architectural public art sculpture made from interwoven twigs and saplings" class="wp-image-476095" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-6-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Happy Go Lucky.&#8221; Image courtesy of Horseshoe Bay Farms</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7.jpg" alt="a whimsical, architectural public art sculpture made from interwoven twigs and saplings amid a wooded area" class="wp-image-476096" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/dougherty-7-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Hopscotch.&#8221; Image courtesy of The Wild Center</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Debra Broz&#8217;s Kitschy &#8216;Superorganisms&#8217; Are Both Familiar and Strange</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/debra-broz-superorganisms-ceramics-found-objects-sculpture/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 22 Jul 2026 19:54:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[animals]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ceramics]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Debra Broz]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[found objects]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476060</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-8.jpg" alt="Debra Broz&#8217;s Kitschy &#8216;Superorganisms&#8217; Are Both Familiar and Strange" />The Seattle-based artist's quirky sculptures are made from from found figurines.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/debra-broz-superorganisms-ceramics-found-objects-sculpture/">Debra Broz&#8217;s Kitschy &#8216;Superorganisms&#8217; Are Both Familiar and Strange</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-8.jpg" alt="Debra Broz&#8217;s Kitschy &#8216;Superorganisms&#8217; Are Both Familiar and Strange" />


<p>In a practice she describes as &#8220;ceramic collage,&#8221; <a href="https://www.debrabroz.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Debra Broz</a> delves into the world of secondhand decor and kitsch. The Seattle-based artist&#8217;s <a href="/tags/debra-broz">quirky sculptures</a> are made from found figurines, which she cuts and reconfigures into playful hybrid forms. &#8220;A lot of times when I look at them, I think about if they were alive, how would they move and how would they operate?&#8221; Broz tells <a href="https://www.youtube.com/@SeattleChannel21" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Seattle Channel</a>.</p>



<p>In her ongoing series <em>Superorganisms, </em>the artist creates three-dimensional assemblages that toy with the boundary between familiarity and the uncanny. &#8220;It&#8217;s really important to me that you look at it and your first thought is, &#8216;That&#8217;s a figurine I&#8217;ve seen before,'&#8221; she says. &#8220;And then your second thought is, &#8216;Wait, that&#8217;s something I&#8217;ve never seen before.'&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2301" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic bird figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476064" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4-640x736.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4-960x1104.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4-768x884.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4-1335x1536.jpg 1335w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-4-1780x2048.jpg 1780w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Biblical Angel 3&#8221; (2026), secondhand ceramics and mixed media, 19 x 14 x 8 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>Broz often finds thematic figurines to work into larger compositions, building a jumbled mound of cats, for example, or all-white horses or rabbits. Overall, the finishes and junctions between individual creatures appear natural enough that one might think they were created that way. In the same vein, that precision works wonders in her adjacent conservation practice called <a href="https://www.scienceofartrestoration.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Science of Restoration</a>, which specializes in ceramics repair.</p>



<p>Three numbered works all sharing the title &#8220;Biblical Angel&#8221; will be on view this weekend in <a href="https://www.antlerpdx.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Antler Gallery</a>’s booth at the <a href="https://seattleartfair.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Seattle Art Fair</a>, which runs from July 23 to 26. See more of the artist&#8217;s process below in the video produced for Seattle Channel.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1836" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic cat figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476066" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6-640x588.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6-960x881.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6-768x705.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-6-1536x1410.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Superorganism (Cat)&#8221; (2025), secondhand ceramic figurines and mixed media, 16 x 20 x 16 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2450" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic bird figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476063" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3-640x784.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3-960x1176.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3-768x941.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3-1254x1536.jpg 1254w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-3-1672x2048.jpg 1672w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Biblical Angel 2&#8221; (2026), secondhand ceramics and mixed media, 18 x 11 x 9 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1317" height="1461" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-5.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic white horse figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476065" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-5.jpg 1317w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-5-640x710.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-5-960x1065.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-5-768x852.jpg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1317px) 100vw, 1317px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Horse Tree&#8221; (2025), secondhand ceramic figurines and mixed media, 14.5 x 9 x 5 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1874" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic dog figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476067" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7-640x600.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7-960x900.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7-768x720.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-7-1536x1439.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Superorganism (Dog)&#8221; (2025), secondhand ceramic figurines, 16 x 17 x 14 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2606" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2.jpg" alt="a ceramic sculpture made using numerous found ceramic bird figurines, assembled together in a jumbled composition" class="wp-image-476062" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2-640x834.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2-960x1251.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2-768x1001.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2-1179x1536.jpg 1179w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/broz-2-1572x2048.jpg 1572w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Biblical Angel 1&#8221; (2026), secondhand ceramics and mixed media, 26 x 19 x 14 inches</figcaption></figure>
